_comment: MEASURED, not authored. Each palette is the output of the product's own
extractEmojiColors() run against the emoji in a real browser — the same
code path the Ward uses when a person picks an avatar.
WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT A GENERATOR STEP: extractEmojiColors renders the
emoji with canvas fillText and reads the pixels back. There is no canvas in
node, so the capture cannot run at build time. The PRESET MATH is still read
from the product's source at every build (tools/build-vignettes.mjs imports
vignettePresets.js itself) — only this capture is held still.
TO RE-CAPTURE, or to add a role: open the Ward on localhost and run
const m = await import('/src/lib/emojiColor.js')
m.extractEmojiColors('<emoji>')
then paste the three {h,s,l} here. The generator THROWS on a role with no
palette, so a new role breaks the build rather than shipping a guess.
'fallback' records whether the extractor fell through to its codepoint-hue
path (it does when a platform renders emoji monochrome to canvas). A true
here means the colour is derived from the codepoint, not from the artwork —
which is a legitimate result but not a measurement of the emoji, so it is
recorded rather than hidden.

PRESET IS PER ROLE. `roles.<name>.preset` picks the treatment; the top-level `preset` is only the fallback for a role that names none. ⛔ Do NOT set them all to one value — the eight presets are per-EMOJI treatments and one across all five makes the set read uniform, which is the failure that got the first pass reverted. Measured 2026-08-23 across all 5x8: emoji-vs-ground contrast ranged 1.7 to 14.0, and the per-cell maximum picks v7 four times out of five, so legibility alone is NOT a sufficient rule — variety is the second axis.

INK GEOMETRY — measured the same way and for the same reason as the palettes. A flex box centres the LINE BOX, not the glyph, and every emoji fills its box by a different amount, so a single font-size makes some badges look small and some look off-centre. Both were real complaints (Jacob, 2026-08-23: the bicycle is 'too small and not optically centered').
inkH  = the glyph's inked height as a fraction of its box. 🚲 is 0.48 where 🌳/🔑 are 0.70 — the bicycle really is ~30% smaller at the same font-size; that is measurement, not perception.
inkDy = how far the ink's centre sits from the box centre (+down). 🚲 is +0.004 where everything else is about -0.09, so it hangs ~0.09 of a box lower than its siblings.

The generator turns these into a per-role scale (toward `inkTarget`) and a nudge, so ANY emoji anyone picks later is sized and centred by its own ink rather than by luck. ⛔ Re-measure when you change an emoji — the same snippet that captures the palette can capture this; see the commit that added it.
